This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .15,00,000/- for the death of Dileep Kumar H.C. S/o Chandregowda in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 24-10-2023, at about 8:30 PM, Dileep Kumar was riding a motorcycle bearing registration KA-54-H-1261 near the Royal Enfield Showroom, Bommanhalli Metro Station, Bengaluru.
While negotiating a road hump, which was constructed in an unscientific manner and lacked proper white lenses or reflectors for night visibility, he lost control of the vehicle and fell.
His helmet was broken, and he sustained grievous head injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to St. John's Hospital for first aid and later shifted to Kshema Hospital,
where he was admitted as an inpatient.
Despite the best efforts of the medical team, he succumbed to his injuries on 02-12-2023 at about 11:30 AM.
Following the post-mortem conducted at Bowring Hospital, the petitioner received the body and performed the last rites.
3. Petitioner No. 1 is the mother and Petitioner No. 2 is the younger brother of the deceased.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 31 years, and employed with Air Tours and Travels, earning a monthly salary of Rs. 30,000.
The petitioners were dependent on the income of the deceased, and due to his untimely death, they have suffered mental shock, agony, and loss of their breadwinner.

The petitioners have also incurred significant expenditure for transportation,
funeral, and related ceremonies.
4. In view of the above, the petitioners seek compensation of Rs. 15,00,000, with interest, from Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 2, being the owner and insurer of the vehicle.
5. In response to the petition notice, Respondent No. 2 appeared through its counsel and filed an objection.
Respondent No. 1 did not appear before the court; hence, the matter proceeded ex parte against Respondent No. 1.
In its objection, Respondent No. 2 admitted the issuance of the insurance policy, but contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Respondent No. 2 alleged that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased, as he was riding the motorcycle at high speed, lost control, and fell.
The police records are said to reflect these facts.

7. Accordingly, it was argued that the deceased was the tortfeasor and did not possess a valid driving license; therefore, the petition is not maintainable as the accident resulted from his own negligence.
Respondent No. 2 also contended that a tortfeasor cannot claim compensation for his own negligence, and that the claimed compensation is highly excessive.
It denied the deceased's occupation, income, relationship with the petitioners, and dependency, and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that Dileep Kumar H.C. S/o.Chandrappa, has died in Road Traffic Accident involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-54-H-1261 on 24-10-2023 at about 8-30 p.m., near Royal Enfield showroom, Bommanahalli metro station, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petition is maintainable?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount?

sentences.text: his helmet was broken.
He sustained grievous head injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to St. John's Hospital and then shifted to Kshema Hospital, where he was admitted as an inpatient.
Despite the best efforts of the medical team, he succumbed to his injuries on 02-12- 2023 at about 11:30 AM.
13. PW-1 further stated that the motorcycle belonged to his father, Respondent No. 1, but the deceased was using the motorcycle.

The insurance premium for the vehicle was regularly paid, and the policy covered third-party and personal accident (PA) coverage of Rs. 15,00,000.
14.

The petitioner relied upon police documents at Ex. P-1 to P-10, including the FIR, complaint,
MLC, police intervention, spot Mahazar, inquest, post- mortem report, IMV report, and charge sheet.
According to the police documents, a charge sheet was filed against the deceased, and the accident arose out of the use of the said motorcycle.
The motorcycle itself, bearing KA-54H-1261 and ridden by the deceased, establishes its involvement in the accident.
15. It is noted that the FIR was filed by the brother of the deceased on 01-12-2023, and the RC owner of the motorcycle was a father of the deceased.
These facts were not disputed by Respondent No. 2.
Respondent No. 2 contended only that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased, arguing that the petition is therefore not maintainable.
PW-1 denied suggestions that the deceased was not wearing a helmet or was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident.
16. As per the post-mortem report, Dileep Kumar died due to head injuries sustained in the accident, and no other cause of death was found.
Respondent No. 2 did not produce any material evidence to suggest an alternate cause of death.
17. In view of the above, it is held that the death of Dileep Kumar was solely due to accidental injuries arising from the use and involvement of the motorcycle bearing KA-54-H-1261.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2:-
It is the specific contention of Respondent No. 2, the Insurance Company, that the present petition is not maintainable.
The Respondent No. 2 contends that the deceased was not the registered owner of the insured vehicle, and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
Consequently, the deceased is not entitled to any compensation under the Personal Accident (PA) coverage class of the policy.

19. It is further submitted that PA coverage is a contractual benefit, confined strictly to the owner-cum- driver of the insured vehicle holding a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident.
To substantiate this, the official of Respondent No. 2 was examined as RW1.
It is an admitted fact that the deceased was not the registered owner of the motorbike; the RC ownership was in the name of his father.
Admittedly, the deceased was riding the motorbike at the time of the accident.

sentences.text: The evidence and record show that deceased neither the RC owner nor named in the insurance policy.
It is well-settled law that PA coverage under a motor insurance policy is available only to the owner and rider of the insured vehicle, and not to any other person.

Even if a person was using or driving the vehicle with the permission of the owner, PA coverage does not constitute a statutory liability under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, but is merely a contractual benefit.
The scope of coverage is strictly restricted to the terms and conditions of the policy.
21. In the present case, the deceased was neither the owner of the insured vehicle nor an authorized rider.
He was merely a borrower and an unauthorized rider.

The petitioners, however, contended that since the deceased had contributed towards the purchase of the motorcycle and had paid the insurance premium from his own funds, he effectively stepped into the shoes of the owner of the motorcycle.

The petitioners relies on the decisions:
 2009 AIR SCW 4916, Ningamma and anr. V United India Insurance Co Ltd.
 2020 ACJ 627: Rama Killadi & Another vs United Insurance Company Ltd &
Another.

sentences.text: 23. Upon perusal of the insurance policy, considering the rival contentions of the parties and the material on record, it is evident that the deceased was not covered under any contractual class extending PA coverage to him.
The policy does not indicate any special endorsement covering unnamed or unauthorized riders.
Therefore, the benefit of PA coverage cannot be extended to the deceased, as he does not fall within the definition of owner or authorized rider under the policy.
24. It is also pertinent to note that the claim petition has been filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
This provision requires proof of negligence on the part of another person.
From the material on record, the accident occurred solely due to the fault of the deceased and not due to any fault of a third party.
Consequently, the petition is not maintainable, as the deceased cannot be considered a borrower or insured rider in the circumstances.
25. In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is of the opinion that: The deceased was not the RC owner of the vehicle.
The deceased was not covered under the PA class of the insurance policy.

sentences.text: Contributions made by the deceased towards the vehicle or premium, while noted, cannot alter the contractual scope of the policy, as the RC ownership remained with his father.
The accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased.
Therefore, the claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is not maintainable.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the negative.
26. ISSUE NO.3:-
In view of my findings on issue No.2, the petitioner are not entitled for any compensation.
Accordingly I answer issue no 3 in the negative.
27. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 2 and 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is dismissed as not maintainable.
Draw award accordingly.
